h1: Three Sukhumvit Hotel — the closest hotel to Bumrungrad International Hospital, two minutes on foot with genuinely spacious rooms
intro: If you need to be in Bangkok for treatment at Bumrungrad International Hospital — whether you are a patient or a family member — the first question is usually which hotel lets you reach the hospital most quickly. Three Sukhumvit Hotel is the answer that comes up most often. This 3-star boutique hotel with 59 rooms sits on Sukhumvit Soi 3, roughly 130 metres — about a 2-minute walk — from Bumrungrad's front entrance. No other hotel in the area is closer. Rooms are meaningfully larger than you would expect at this price point, and rates start from approx. THB 1,600/night. The overall score is 8.3 from 88 reviews on Trip.com.

body.html: Three Sukhumvit Hotel has one clear advantage and it is a significant one: the distance from the hotel lobby to Bumrungrad International Hospital's entrance is approximately 130 metres — a flat, straightforward walk of about 2 minutes. Turn left out of the lobby on Soi 3 and the hospital gate is already in view. For a patient with an early appointment, for a family member making multiple trips in a day, or for anyone arriving late and exhausted from a long flight ahead of treatment, cutting out the taxi entirely is not a minor convenience — it is the whole point.

The rooms are what guests praise most after the location. The Superior rooms run around 35 sq m and the Deluxe rooms around 40 sq m — both comfortably above the Bangkok three-star average. Several reviews describe their room as feeling "like an upgrade" compared with what they expected. The Junior Suites at 45 sq m add a proper sitting area with a sofa, which works well for families staying a few days or for anyone who needs to rest in between hospital appointments without being confined to a bed.
"The room was spacious and clean, and walking to Bumrungrad only took two minutes — for anyone going back and forth to the hospital all day, a location like this makes a real difference."

Practical amenities are solid for a three-star property. Free parking is genuinely rare on this stretch of Sukhumvit and particularly useful for families driving in from other provinces. Free Wi-Fi throughout the property, a restaurant, room service, luggage storage, taxi booking through the concierge desk and a 24-hour front desk are all standard. Continental breakfast is available for an additional fee of around THB 400 per person, though reviews suggest the value is questionable at that price — the surrounding streets of Soi 3 have far better and cheaper options for the same morning meal.

The hotel has been operating since 2006, with a renovation in 2013, and the age shows in places. The lobby and some common areas feel dated compared with newer properties in the same price bracket. This is not a deal-breaker if you are primarily coming for the proximity to Bumrungrad, but it is worth knowing going in so expectations are set correctly. Some rooms on the street-facing side of the building pick up traffic noise from Soi 3, especially in the evenings when the nearby restaurants and street activity pick up.

BTS Nana station is around 800 metres away — approximately a 10-minute walk, or a short motorbike-taxi ride for a few tens of baht. The immediate neighbourhood of Sukhumvit Soi 3 is known for Middle Eastern restaurants, convenience stores and a handful of cafes, all within easy walking distance. For anyone whose primary reason for being in Bangkok is Bumrungrad Hospital, there is simply no other accommodation in the area that offers the same combination of short walking distance, spacious rooms and free parking at this price level.

Tips from the reviews: request a quiet room away from the street-facing side when booking, particularly if you are a light sleeper or need proper rest during recovery. Book well in advance during the high season (November to February) — the hotel has only 59 rooms and the medical-travel clientele tends to book them repeatedly. If you are arriving by car from another province, the free parking alone is worth factoring into your choice.

honestSummary: Three Sukhumvit Hotel makes the most sense for patients and families who need to be as close as possible to Bumrungrad International Hospital — its 130-metre distance from the hospital entrance, larger-than-average rooms and free parking are a hard combination to beat in this area at this price. Just be clear that this is not a new or luxurious property; the common areas are ageing and some rooms face a noisy street.
honestChecks: If you want a new, modern hotel with fresh interiors and full facilities — Three Sukhumvit opened in 2006 and was last renovated in 2013; the lobby shows its age → if newer surroundings matter, look at more recently built hotels in the Sukhumvit 3–11 corridor.

If you are not visiting Bumrungrad and want a lively, walkable base for exploring Bangkok — BTS Nana is around 800 m away and the Soi 3 neighbourhood is quiet compared with Thong Lor or Asok → if you want nightlife and malls on your doorstep, consider those areas instead.
If you are a light sleeper or recovering from treatment — some rooms face Sukhumvit Soi 3, which gets noisy in the evenings → tell the hotel you want a quiet room on the interior side when you book.

tips.title: Tell the hotel about any medical needs
tips.body: The hotel is well used to medical-travel guests and has flexible policies for patients — the concierge can arrange hospital transfers and hold luggage during appointments. Contact them in advance.

tips.title: Request a quiet room when booking
tips.body: Ask specifically for a room not facing Soi 3 — particularly important if you are a light sleeper or recovering from treatment. The interior-facing rooms are noticeably quieter.

tips.title: Skip the hotel breakfast — eat on Soi 3 instead
tips.body: The street outside has Thai restaurants, Arabic eateries and cafes open from early morning — cheaper and better than the hotel's THB 400 continental breakfast.

tips.title: Book ahead in high season
tips.body: With only 59 rooms and a regular medical-travel clientele, the hotel fills fast in November to February — book in advance and pick a free-cancellation rate to stay flexible.

faq.q: How far is Three Sukhumvit Hotel from Bumrungrad International Hospital?
faq.a: The hotel is approximately 130 metres — about a 2-minute walk — from Bumrungrad International Hospital's front entrance. Turn left out of the lobby on Soi 3 and the hospital gate is already visible. It is the closest hotel in the immediate area to the hospital.

faq.q: How much does Three Sukhumvit Hotel cost per night?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 1,600/night for a Superior room in low season. Deluxe rooms run around THB 2,000 and Junior Suites around THB 2,600. Prices rise during the high season (November to February), so booking ahead pays off.

faq.q: Is Three Sukhumvit Hotel near BTS Nana?
faq.a: BTS Nana station is approximately 800 metres away, or about a 10-minute walk. A motorbike taxi from the hotel to Nana BTS takes just a few minutes and costs around THB 20–30. For guests focused primarily on Bumrungrad rather than daily BTS travel, this distance is manageable.

faq.q: Who is Three Sukhumvit Hotel best suited for?
faq.a: It is best suited for patients, family members of patients and medical tourists visiting Bumrungrad International Hospital, as well as families who drive in from other provinces and need free parking in the Sukhumvit area.

faq.q: Does Three Sukhumvit Hotel have free parking?
faq.a: Yes — the hotel offers free parking, which is a genuine rarity on this stretch of Sukhumvit. It is a particularly useful advantage for families driving in from other Thai provinces for treatment at Bumrungrad.
